title: Chapter 86: The Last Classroom
html:
The voyeur was Fan Yu’s father?Without those notes, Chen Ge would never have imagined it. I was right. Fan Yu’s aunt hid something crucial from me.

Earlier, his attempt to identify the killer had lacked one crucial element: motive. The notes opened a new line of inquiry.

Three notes in three different hands. At least three people knew Teacher Fan’s filthy secret.Chen Ge left the notes inside the book. Age had made the paper fragile, and a careless touch might destroy vital evidence.

The handwriting is clear. Teacher Fan probably kept the notes so he could compare them with the students’ work and identify the writers. Mu Yang High School was small; as a member of staff, three days would have been plenty of time to inspect everyone’s handwriting.

Chen Ge committed the notes to memory. He wondered how the three students had discovered the cubicle’s secret. Were they all victims? The tone doesn’t fit, especially the last line—If you insist on staying at this school, then you shall stay here forever. That doesn’t sound like a victim speaking.

The notes’ message was clear, but their demand struck Chen Ge as naive. Someone like Fan Yu’s father should have been reported to the police, not pressured into a public apology. Public exposure might only deepen the victim’s trauma.

These notes do sound as though students wrote them. Could those students have thrown Teacher Fan into the well?

He had a motive now, but the timing made no sense. Two adults had disappeared that night. Killing both and disposing of their bodies without a trace seemed beyond several teenagers.

I’m missing something.Chen Ge considered the situation from Teacher Fan’s perspective. A public apology was out of the question; exposure would ruin his life. He already had a record before coming to Mu Yang High School, and a repeat offense would bring severe punishment.

Fan Yu’s father knew that, which was why he had kept the notes. He likely intended to identify the students who threatened him and silence them himself, but his three-day search appeared to have failed.

So this is what I know. Three different students wrote the notes, yet Teacher Fan could not identify them by comparing their handwriting with the school’s records. They discovered the sixth cubicle’s secret, but instead of going to the police, they chose the least effective and most revealing approach: threatening him directly. And the final warning came true.

None of it made sense. In summary, three students whom no one could identify discovered Teacher Fan’s voyeurism and, when their warning failed, made him disappear.

No ordinary person could meet all three conditions.Chen Ge had a strong suspicion about the killer’s identity, but he was not yet certain.

The notes also mention a girl whom they want Fan Yu’s father to apologize to. If I can find her, then many problems will be solved.

After recording everything with his camera, Chen Ge shut the book and placed it back where it had been.

If I hadn’t searched every drawer, I never would have found the notes hidden in this book. Every mystery is solved through details.

Chen Ge exited the mathematics room and went through the other rooms but came up with nothing.

It’s already ten thirty. At this pace, I won’t finish the last two side missions.Chen Ge left the office with his flashlight and searched the grounds for the well. Even after an hour in the rain, he found nothing.

Where could the well be? The black phone can’t be wrong.Chen Ge’s pants and shoes were drenched, and exhaustion showed in his face.

Only half an hour until midnight. I’ll have to abandon the well mission and find shelter.Head bowed against the rain, Chen Ge walked toward the education block. He wanted to reach the sealed classroom before midnight, but if the mission proved too dangerous, he would give it up.

Water weighed down his boots, and every step left a distinct print. Inside the education block, he went straight to the sealed classroom. Through its window, the lone table at the center—with textbook, pen, and paper neatly arranged—looked profoundly unnatural.

It looks stranger than I expected.

Mu Yang High School had originally been a crematorium. Chen Ge read from the online threads that the sealed classroom was exactly the location of the crematorium’s former morgue. It had powerful Yin energy, and that was why the headmaster had kept the classroom sealed.

One story claimed a school bus had crashed during a class trip, killing many students. Their spirits returned to school, and the headmaster kept this room open to accommodate them.

The final explanation was the most uplifting. Before its closure, Mu Yang High School had ranked first in Jiujiang—counting from the bottom. Some teachers proposed sorting classes by grades, with the worst performers placed farthest back. The headmaster vetoed the idea and sealed the last classroom as a reminder that no one was born to be last, and labeling students that way would be a terrible mistake.

Many other rumors surrounded the sealed classroom, but these were the three Chen Ge remembered hearing most often.

He checked the time again. At 11:36 p.m., he opened the door and entered. Moving quickly, he headed straight for the objects on the center table.

The classroom felt no different from the corridor, save perhaps for a deeper silence.

Chen Ge looked at the textbook and the paper, but there was nothing notable written on them. However, when he picked up the textbook, he discovered there was plenty of writing carved into the wooden table.
